market_name: Israel x Turkey military clash before 2027?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability move is accompanied by any wire headlines (Reuters/AP) on Israel-Turkey friction over Syria; confirm TUR/lira are reacting and the move isn't idle market noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare TUR move vs broad EM ETF (EEM) to isolate Turkey-specific risk; watch USDTRY for confirmation of FX channel.
time_plan.2h: Re-assess if probability move holds or fades; check Turkish CDS and Borsa Istanbul futures for corroboration.
time_plan.6h: Look for official statements from Ankara/Jerusalem; if no escalation confirmation, expect mean reversion in TUR.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate whether the signal translated into a durable Turkey-specific repricing or was noise; close out thesis assessment.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a direct Israel-Turkey military clash would raise Turkish geopolitical/escalation risk premia. Turkish assets (lira, equities) are already fragile and highly sensitive to geopolitical stress; an escalation signal would pressure TUR lower via risk-off, FX weakness (TUR is USD-denominated so lira depreciation compounds losses), and foreign outflows. TUR is the most liquid pure Turkey proxy. Most realistic moves from a probability shift alone are modest (sub-700bps) unless an actual kinetic incident occurs, so this likely falls below the tradable threshold.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check if Brent/WTI are moving in tandem with the probability shift or driven by unrelated inventory/OPEC news.
time_plan.1h: Assess whether broader Middle East risk assets (gold, VIX) confirm a risk premium story vs isolated noise.
time_plan.2h: Look for tanker-route or Eastern Mediterranean shipping disruption reports that would justify a supply premium.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether oil premium persists or fades absent a concrete incident.
time_plan.12h: Determine whether the oil move was conflict-driven or coincidental; finalize assessment.

predictions.reasoning: A material rise in Israel-Turkey conflict probability adds to Middle East war-risk premium, which can bid crude on supply-disruption fears (shipping lanes, broader regional spillover). However Turkey and Israel are not major oil producers, so the direct supply linkage is weak; the channel is sentiment/regional-contagion rather than physical barrels. This makes the signal noisy and low-confidence, likely sub-700bps unless an actual incident materializes.

evidence_used: Market question on direct Israel-Turkey military clash by end-2026
Known fragility and geopolitical sensitivity of Turkish lira and equities
General pattern of Middle East escalation risk boosting oil and gold
Liquidity profiles of TUR and USO as the most accessible proxies
uncertainty_notes: This is a long-dated (through 2026) market; a 12h probability move may reflect speculation rather than imminent events.
Prediction-market probability shifts rarely map to >700bps ETF moves absent an actual kinetic incident.
Turkey and Israel are minor oil producers, so the crude linkage is contagion/sentiment-based and weak.
The signal could already be public (news-driven) rather than leaked information.

llm_justification.summary: A sharp increase in the implied probability of a direct Israel-Turkey military clash would most cleanly pressure Turkish risk assets (TUR lower via equity decline and lira weakness) and secondarily add a modest Middle East war-risk premium to oil. Both channels are real but likely sub-700bps unless an actual military incident occurs, so neither clears the tradable threshold on a probability move alone. Confidence is moderate-to-low given the long horizon and the market's role as a noisy sensor.
key_assumptions: A probability move is sharp and conflict-specific, not general EM/risk noise.
Turkish assets remain the most directly exposed liquid proxy.
No prior public news has already fully priced the escalation risk.
failure_modes: The probability move reverses quickly as speculation fades, with no real-world corroboration.
The information is already public (news-driven), so assets have already repriced before the signal.
TUR/USO are weak or mis-specified proxies—Turkey-Israel tensions may hit specific names (defense, airlines) or FX more than broad ETFs.
Oil shows no reaction because neither country is a material producer and no supply route is threatened.
Risk-off could paradoxically strengthen USD/safe havens in ways that offset expected directional moves.
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
